flows:
Navigate to http://127.0.0.1:4173/ then Open Hati with no saved data (clear this site's browser storage and reload if any bills or people exist).
Add the people Ana, Ben and Cy.
Click Add bill and enter the name Rent.
Enter the amount 1,000.00 and choose Ana with an equal split.
Enter the amount 1,000.00 and choose Ben with an equal split.
Enter the amount 1,000.00 and choose Cy with an equal split.
Save the bill and look at each person's share of the bill.
Assert Ana's share shows 333.34.
Assert Ben's share shows 333.33.
Assert Cy's share shows 333.33.
Get the shares shown for Ana, Ben and Cy, in that order, as one comma-separated line and save as {{equal_split_shares}}.

wait: queued plan (2 steps): type "Name"; click "Add person"
wait: queued plan (2 steps): type "Name"; click "Add person"
type: Typing Rent into Bill name field
wait: queued plan (5 steps): type "Amount"; click "Ana"; click "Ben"; click "Cy"; clic

wait: PRIMARY: look at each person's share of the bill
analyze: ANALYZE(textual_visual, 'The shares shown for Ana, Ben and Cy, in that order, ar

summary:
Started Hati with no saved information, then added Ana, Ben, and Cy.
Created and saved a Rent bill for 1,000.00, paid by Ana, using an equal split among all three people.
Reviewed the saved bill: Ana's share is 333.34, Ben's share is 333.33, and Cy's share is 333.33.
The requested bill and all three displayed shares were saved successfully.
one_liner: created and reviewed an equally split Rent bill on Hati

equal_split_shares.code_js: (() => { const text = el(43).innerText; const matches = [...text.matchAll(/(?:Ana|Ben|Cy)\s+(\d+\.\d{2})/g)]; return matches.length === 3 ? matches.map(m => m[1]).join(',') : null; })()
